General/Miscellaneous

The Michigan Department of Natural Resources (MIDNR) will conduct its annual fall lake trout survey in Lake Superior between Big Bay and Grand Island from October 19, 2026, through November 6, 2026. Operations will be conducted aboard the Research Vessel Lake Char.
Survey operations involve deploying bottom-set gill nets approximately 1,200 feet in length, extending six feet from the lakebed, and remaining set overnight in waters generally under 100 feet deep within a few miles of shore. Net locations include waters off Big Bay Point, Salmon Trout Point, Garlic Island Reef, Yellow Dog Point, Thoney Point, Granite Island, Granite Point, Partridge Island Reef, Presque Isle Harbor, Wood Island, Wood Island Shoal, and Trout Point Reef.
All nets are marked with black and orange flagged staff buoys labeled with agency identification.
The R/V Lake Char will monitor VHF-FM

The Coast Guard has transitioned to a visual Maritime Safety Information Products application for the transmission of relevant information previously contained in the published Local Notice to Mariners and Coast Guard Light List. The application, which is accessible at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi, contains the most up to date maritime information overlayed on nautical charts and plotted using latitude and longitude. While the ability to print Local Notice to Mariners and Light List copies is still temporarily available, these printed products lack the positional accuracy of the electronic application and can therefore lead to relevant information being overlooked. Operations will take place from October 1, 2026 through November 15, 2026, daily from 0700 to 1900 (Monday through Sunday).
The Tug General, along with barges MM 142 and DB12, will be working on spuds within the marina. Operations will be located primarily within 500 feet of the marina. Additional barges may be moored to an anchor can buoy located northwest of Little Sand Bay Marina at coordinates 46° 56' 56.24" N, 090° 53' 40.21" W.
